english_verification.review_scope: Read the J53 history template, opening Zabutodask mission block, native English country-name localisation, and selected English flavour passages on steppe pastoralism, water policy, and the centaur choices. Read the actual Lake Federation chunk containing the Orachav passage (part 5, not the opening chunk) for related later-Kalsyto context. Confirmed the source distinction between the J53 formable and a fixed 1444 country. Bounded text verification only; no mission-tree audit. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: No dedicated J53 Wiki country page was found in the offline query; the Lake Federation page is related historical context only.
The read Orachav passage describes a later Kalsyto context; it does not establish J53's 1444 history.
Formation year and campaign-specific route timing are not fixed.

rationale.campaign_length: 35 J53-exclusive definitions, plus shared Lake Federation content.
rationale.colonization: There is steppe settlement, but no overseas colonization focus.
rationale.complexity: Formation, religion, steppe governance, and branching wars run in parallel.
rationale.dark_story: The extermination branch is extremely dark; the reconciliation branch is its opposite.
rationale.difficulty: Formation and frontier wars require planning; no hands-on difficulty test was performed.
rationale.diplomacy: Choose among peace, vassalage, and war with centaurs and southern states.
rationale.early_pressure: Pressure depends on the Lake Federation predecessor and the breakup situation.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Theology matters, but ordinary firearms are not artificery.
rationale.narrative_density: The Federation's breakup, steppe revival, and the centaur choice are linked.
rationale.tall_play: Pastoralism and water management matter, but this is not a single-city campaign.
rationale.trade_economy: A grassland economy supports a cavalry state.
rationale.warfare: Steppe cavalry and later southern campaigns define the core loop.

identity.appearance: A Lake Federation breakup formable, not a fixed 1444 landholder.
identity.formation_scope: Eligible Lake Federation members can trigger J53 formation during the breakup; the Tag and mission tree change, but the year is not fixed.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: While the modern Triunics may appear otherwise, the Zabatlari were once numerous nomadic groups that lived across the entire steppe. While many techniques have since been forgotten, the capacity to recover them has lingered in our blood. With those adventurous at heart joining us to forge a new identity on the plains as the Orachav, it is only a matter of time before the lands belong to us again.

description.text:
While the goddesses of the lakes are closely associated with the Triunics, they were not the first gods worshiped by our people. Inscribed on ruins across the endless grasslands are the rites of our forefathers, and highest among them are those towards Taqoshur, the sun above our heads and the source of all life and civilization.
While it was behind mother Yukel's waves that we bided our time, it is under Taqoshur's glow that we face our destiny head-on.

description.text: While the forests, hills, and cities of Leloyal inhibited the movements of cavalry, the open steppe demands the free movement only a mount can provide. While we have yet to master this form, you need only look to a pack of centaurs to learn the role of mobility in combat. To have your enemy surrounded is to have effectively won a battle before it has even begun, and to retain the ability to flee from an advancing foe ensures total defeat is an impossibility. Let no Orachav fight with their feet upon the ground, and they will never be vanquished.

description.text: As we reclaim our own ancestral lands from those that took it from us, the stout inhabitants of the mountains surrounding us have begun to do the same. Tayoghor, a god of such proportions, embodies this desire to protect our lands from that which threaten it, and to enrich ourselves from the bounty of our land. Any who fight against the forces of evil and disaster are a friend to the Orachav, and any skilled warrior can find a home among us.

description.text: When a lone Orachav travels, knowing how much food to carry can be a matter of life and death, for the nearest supplies could be days away. When a group travels, herd animals may be brought along, but in the haste of war this luxury cannot be afforded. While horses can tilt their necks and feast upon grass at a moment's notice, our men must be prepared for weeks of travel and know how to prepare for it.

description.text: While the physically stronger centaur has been the master of hectic warfare, the introduction of the firearm has returned the advantage to us. Their charges across the field of battle mean little now that we can drop them dead from a distance, which we can maintain upon our own steeds. While some have learned to fire a bow from atop a horse, the effectiveness of the gun will multiply that technique tenfold.

description.text: Yerush teaches us that while the lands of the steppe may be consistent, the wars needed to defend it are anything but. When terrain is not limited, the formations of friend and foe alike. The flares and smoke of our fellow men's Budakh Brigades, the endless harassment of a centaur Taryean Raider party, or the Ogrish bulk of an Armed Iklomgemar, we must be prepared to adapt to and vanquish them all.

description.text: When the Great Incursion reached our city the centaurs met their match, our city being built atop a great plateau that they could not scale. Even faced with such an obstacle they, perhaps admirably, persisted, leaving thousands of their warriors slain by our archers below our towers. Thanks to their stubbornness we have plenty of materiel to fertilize our fields with.

description.text: Yikashlay was founded by a mysterious sorcerer known as "He of the Horizon", who raised the plateau our city rests upon and constructing many of the towers our people call home. Quite a few of the towers are still barely used, allowing us to convert them to whatever purposes we require.

description.text: The centaur hordes must have been attempting to starve us out of our towers. How they must have wept when we simply began growing our produce from our tallest towers.

description.text: There are those that would call our dignitaries "vulgar" and "crude", but it is they that simply cannot take a goodnatured joke.

description.text: As our plateau runs out of space to construct towers upon and our standing edifices fill with workshops and residences, we have taken to expanding into the rock beneath our city, establishing a bustling market carved within the very bedrock.

description.text: Our city offers a view like none other, granting an unobstructed view of the stars above at night, which our scholars have taken to meticulously tracking and charting.
description.text_en: Our city offers a view like none other, granting an unobstructed view of the stars above at night, which our scholars have taken to meticulously tracking and charting.

description.text: Our towers are full, and the land beneath risks collapsing should we carve any further. We have only one way to expand; to the very clouds above our towers.

description.text: The western half of our city was utterly devastated by the centaur hordes during the Great Incursion. Much work must be done to return prosperity to this district.
description.text_en: The western half of our city was utterly devastated by the centaur hordes during the Great Incursion. Much work must be done to return prosperity to this district.

description.text: The Sovkokeya is the most commonly used trade ship in Lake Yukelqur, prized for its spacious hold capable of carrying trade goods and men alike.

description.text: To keep smugglers from choking our canal we've organized a militia of marines to patrol the banks. In times of war we can assign these marines to bolster our naval forces.

description.text: The O.M.A. is an organization dedicated to ensuring our hired blades are doing the jobs they were hired for to the best of their ability, and spend their earnings on improving their equipment rather than on drink and women. While some may see this as overbearing our budget certainly appreciates it.

description.text: As our city expands we have taken to constructing great towers linked with bridges crossing over the canal, our wealthy have packed up and moved to this soaring district and many merchants choose to spend long periods of shore leave within the establishments gracing the Sky Walk.

description.text: While our city soars, those left below, quite literally in the dark, toil within the polluted detritus of our undercity. While they may be rowdy brutes, they do bring a certain set of skills to our militia.

description.text: To guide ships through our now darkened canal, the Lightbearers carry torches along the way. They act as our enforcers within the undercity, keeping the scum and rabble out of sight from visiting traders.

description.text: Buruvaqoyla plays host to the legendary mercenary band, the Jolgik Uts. Originally exiles from the islands sent to die fighting the centaurs, since our city's founding they've become a disciplined and respected force of centaur slayers.
description.text_en: Buruvaqoyla plays host to the legendary mercenary band, the Jolgik Uts. Originally exiles from the islands sent to die fighting the centaurs, since our city's founding they've become a disciplined and respected force of centaur slayers.

description.text: Every man must be ready to take up arms and fend off the centaur raids that plague our hinterlands on a yearly basis. Such is life so close to the hordelands.
description.text_en: Every man must be ready to take up arms and fend off the centaur raids that plague our hinterlands on a yearly basis. Such is life so close to the hordelands.

description.text: With the backing of the Federation, we can finally extend our reach beyond our borders into the old lands of our forefathers, taking back the lands our ancestors were forced to flee when the centaurs bore down on them.
description.text_en: With the backing of the Federation, we can finally extend our reach beyond our borders into the old lands of our forefathers, taking back the lands our ancestors were forced to flee when the centaurs bore down on them.

description.text: When one has but a moment's rest to admire the land around them, they can fully recognize the serene and comforting landscape we find ourselves in. If we must fall, we cannot imagine a more scenic place to do so.
description.text_en: When one has but a moment's rest to admire the land around them, they can fully recognize the serene and comforting landscape we find ourselves in. If we must fall, we cannot imagine a more scenic place to do so.

description.text: The Jolgik Uts that founded our city were led by the legendary Lady of Buruvaqoyla. Her origins are a mystery, some claim she was but a former bandit from the northern cities, others suggest that she was a disinherited princess. Whatever her background truly was, we are determined to ensure her dream never falls.

description.text: We finally have the opportunity to subject the dreaded centaurs to the horrors they've inflicted upon us for so long, hunting them in their homes and razing their villages as they did so many times to our hinterlands.

description.text: The Forbidden Plains are vast, a seemingly endless expanse of grass and sand. Led by our fearless Jolgik Uts, our armies have learned to navigate this land like no other.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid this if you want a smooth Lake Federation unification or do not want complex formation conditions and a frontier extermination route.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Form amid the breakup and establish yourself on the steppe; govern the land and revive the faith; then use cavalry and firearms in campaigns while deciding how to deal with centaurs and southern states.
player_overview.overview: The Great Riders are not a starting country, but a steppe republic that may emerge from the Lake Federation's breakup. Make pastoralism and frontier institutions sustain your cavalry, then expand through a new theology, firearm-equipped horsemen, and southern campaigns. The sharpest fork concerns the centaurs: end generations of reprisals, or hunt down the refugees. That choice defines the country more than combat strength alone.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy cavalry republics, an alternate Lake Federation route, and consequential branching choices.
signature_features: A rider republic formed through the Lake Federation's breakup, not its normal unification route.
Pastoralism, steppe faith, and firearm-equipped cavalry shape the state.
Reconciliation or extermination of the centaurs radically changes the country's values and ending.
player_overview.tagline: Lead the Lake's riders back onto the steppe, then choose reconciliation or annihilation as the end of an old feud.

reasons: An unusual formable born from the Lake Federation's breakup.
Cavalry, pastoralism, and theology develop together.
The centaur route creates a stark values divide.
warnings: Formation requirements and the timing of the mission-tree change can be confusing.

positive_indicators: An event offers reconciliation as a way to end generations of reprisals.
Steppe pastoralism and water management support the population's survival.
The mission narrative recognizes sunlight's benefit to different peoples.
values.rationale: Steppe life, republican government, and the option of peace serve the public good. The alternative branch explicitly pursues fleeing centaurs and gravely denies their personhood. The combined score is provisional while the branch is undecided; cavalry conquest alone is not evidence of good or evil.
red_flags: An optional route explicitly proposes continuing to exterminate fleeing centaurs.
Frontier warfare can reduce an entire hostile population to objects.
